caption:
🔥 बॉलीवुड के रॉकिंग स्टार यश को लेकर आ गई है एकदम चटपटी खबर!

🎬 आने वाली मेगा-फिल्म Ramayana में यश रावण का दमदार रोल निभा रहे हैं और Monster Mind Creations के जरिए इसके प्रोड्यूसिंग पार्टनर भी हैं।

👶 यश ने हाल ही में खुलासा किया कि जब उनके बेटे को रामायण की कहानी पता चली, तो वह हैरान रह गया और उसने पूछा कि आप बैड गाय क्यों हैं और आप ऐसा कैसे कर सकते हैं।

💡 यश ने अपने बेटे को समझाया कि पूरी कहानी दिखाने के लिए ऐसा करना पड़ता है और असली जीत हमेशा Lord Rama के रास्ते पर चलने से ही मिलती है।

🎭 यश ने बेटे को यह भी समझाया कि वह थिएटर में एक एक्टर के तौर पर उनके लिए चीयर कर सकता है, लेकिन किरदार को ही असली आदर्श नहीं समझना चाहिए।

💀 इसके बाद बेटे ने पूछा कि क्या कहानी के अंत में उनकी मौत हो जाती है और क्या वे हार जाते हैं, जिसे लेकर यश ने बताया कि प्रोजेक्ट साइन करते वक्त उन्होंने बच्चों के ऐसे सवालों के बारे में नहीं सोचा था।

📅 Nitesh Tiwari के डायरेक्शन में बन रही Ramayana दो पार्ट की एपिक फिल्म है, जिसे Namit Malhotra के Prime Focus Studios और यश की Monster Mind Creations मिलकर बना रहे हैं।

🌍 इस फिल्म का पहला पार्ट 5 नवंबर 2026 को दुनिया भर के सिनेमाघरों में रिलीज होने के लिए शेड्यूल किया गया है!

💬 क्या आपको लगता है कि यश का रावण वाला अवतार पर्दे पर इतिहास रचेगा? जल्दी से कमेंट करके बताओ!

ctx.title: Yash Recalls His Son’s Reaction To Him Playing Ravana In Ramayana: “You’re The Bad Guy! How Can You Do That?”
ctx.summary:
Yash Recalls His Son’s Reaction To Him Playing Ravana In Ramayana: “You’re The Bad Guy! How Can You Do That?” 
 The post  Yash Recalls His Son’s Reaction To Him Playing Ravana In Ramayana: “You’re The Bad Guy! How Can You Do That?”  appeared first on  Koimoi .
ctx.text:
Rocking Star Yash , who essays the role of Ravana in Ramayana and is also a producing partner on the ambitious two-part epic through Monster Mind Creations, recently opened up about one of the most unexpected conversations he had while preparing for the film – explaining to his young son why his father was playing the antagonist and not Lord Rama.
Sharing how his son reacted after learning about the epic, Yash revealed that the little one was initially shocked to discover that his father would be portraying Ravana. He recalled, “My son knows who his father is, but now that he knows the story of the Ramayana, he was shocked. He said, ‘No, you’re the bad guy! How can you do that?’ I explained to him that we have to depict the full story for people to truly understand it.”
Talking about the dilemma of helping his children understand the distinction between the actor and the character, Yash shared how he had to explain the larger significance of the story and why Lord Rama remains the ideal to look up to.
He said, “I had to sit my son down and tell him: in this story, the central figure you must look up to is Lord Rama. Everyone should walk Rama’s path. Ravana may appear grand, powerful, and imposing, but true, lasting victory in life only comes when you embody Rama’s righteousness. I told him, ‘You can cheer for me as an actor in the theatre, but do not mistake the character for the ideal.’”
The conversation took another turn when his son asked him whether Ravana eventually loses and dies in the story. Recalling the moment, Yash said, “Then he asked, ‘Do you die in the end? Do you lose?’ That was hard. When I signed the project, I was thinking about giving my audience a compelling performance, but I hadn’t anticipated my son’s questions. Teaching him the distinction between an actor and a dramatic role was quite an experience.”
With Yash essaying the formidable role of Ravana in Ramayana and also serving as a producing partner through Monster Mind Creations, his account offers an interesting insight into the conversations the epic continues to inspire across generations and how the story’s characters can leave a lasting impression on audiences.
Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with Yash’s Monster Mind Creations. The first instalment of the two-part epic is scheduled for a worldwide theatrical release on November 5, 2026.
